This wave of action serves as practical proof that hosting such sites constitutes an illegal act, directly contradicting the operators' previous assertions that they could operate within legal loopholes by avoiding centralized storage of infringing files.", "summary": "European police raids and voluntary closures dismantle major P2P link sites, proving hosting is illegal."}, "1": {"original": "Decided to voluntarily close its BitTorrent link section after news of admin ar", "rephrased": "Following reports of arrests for administrators of other prominent peer-to-peer sites and receiving formal legal warnings, the operators of the Slovenian-based SuprNova.org decided to voluntarily shut down the section of their website hosting BitTorrent links. While the site's discussion forums and IRC network will remain accessible, the platform will no longer distribute links to copyrighted files, a decision made to avoid further legal consequences in the face of increasing enforcement pressure.", "summary": "SuprNova.org voluntarily closed its BitTorrent links after arrests of other admins and legal warnings."}, "2": {"original": "eXeem, a decentralized BitTorrent project by SuprNova.org, reached beta in lat", "rephrased": "In an effort to circumvent the legal vulnerabilities associated with centralized link sites, the decentralized BitTorrent project eXeem, developed by the creators of SuprNova.org, reached its beta stage at the end of 2004. This initiative aimed to eliminate the need for external torrent link sites and trackers by allowing users to easily publish and distribute new files directly on the network without relying on dedicated servers, thereby attempting to resolve the legal issues that led to the closure of its parent organization's link site.", "summary": "The decentralized eXeem project was developed to eliminate reliance on centralized link sites."}, "3": {"original": "Site closed at about the same time as other raids, reason unknown.", "rephrased": "The torrent site TorrentBits.org was closed around the same time as other major link sites in Europe, yet the specific reasons for its shutdown remain unknown. Unlike some contemporaneous sites that were taken down by police raids or voluntarily closed due to legal pressure, the circumstances surrounding the disappearance of TorrentBits.org have not been clarified, leaving the precise cause of its cessation ambiguous.", "summary": "TorrentBits.org closed around the same time as other raids, but the reason remains unknown."}}
